newsitem.title: UK: East Midlands off high in absence of raid.
newsitem.headline: East Midlands off high in absence of raid.

text.p: Shares in East Midlands Electricity were higher on Monday, but off the day's best levels as the much anticipated dawn raid by Dominion Resources failed to materialise, dealers said.
By 1027 GMT, East Midlands shares were 10p higher at 603-1/2p after having climbed as high as 615p earlier.
"People are still waiting for something to happen," said one. "You can't expect nothing to happen in this sector."
Weekend press reports suggested that the U.S. utility firm, which already expressed interest in East Midlands, would launch a 1.3 billion stg bid this morning.
According to the reports, the offer could value the UK regional electricity company at around 650p per share.
Last week, Dominion said it would not pay much more than 608p per shares. East Midlands, in turn, advised shareholders to reject such an offer as inadequate.
Weekend reports suggested East Midlands' board will hold out for a price of roughly 700p per share, a level analysts have said is closer to East Midlands' true value.
